clue.text: Sweet shower short time later, leading to end of drought

parts.note: to pepper is to shower, as with shot or questions
MIN is short for minute

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, here of drought

explanation.surface: A rain shower arrives a little later and ends a dry spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shower' reads as rain but is the verb to pepper; 'later, leading to' just strings the pieces together, the final T coming from 'end of drought'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mint-flavoured confection is a classic sweet, i.e. a candy.

clue.text: European wine-cellar provided for event

parts.note: a Pole is a native of Poland, a European
a vault is an underground cellar for storing wine

explanation.surface: A European wine cellar has been laid on for some occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an athletics field event in which competitors clear a high bar using a long pole.

clue.text: Fuel, one gathered by Paddy?

explanation.surface: Fuel collected by an Irishman.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddy is a familiar name for an Irishman; turf cut from Irish bogs is a traditional fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Decomposed bog vegetation is dug and dried as a household fuel, notably in Ireland, where 'Paddy' stands for any Irishman.

clue.text: Occasion for making the sign of the cross

definitions.text: Occasion for making the sign of the cross

parts.words: Occasion for making the sign of the cross
parts.note: the surface suggests a religious gesture, but the cross is the X marked on a ballot paper

explanation.walkthrough: Voters mark their choice with an X, a cross, so a poll is when people make that sign.
explanation.definitionFit: At a poll voters put a cross beside their chosen candidate.

clue.text: Gourd, look, in pieces

indicators.note: in shows the word for look sits inside the word for pieces

parts.note: chess pieces are called men
LO is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Look at a gourd broken into pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in pieces' looks like an anagram signal, but 'pieces' is MEN (chessmen) and 'in' puts LO inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This fruit belongs to the gourd family, along with squashes and cucumbers.

clue.text: Second rising in sound is offensive

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the word for sound

parts.note: a noise is a sound

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word for second is read upwards, back to front

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A second rise in the noise level is unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns MO into OM, which 'in' puts inside NOISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something noxious or disgusting, especially in smell, is offensive.

clue.text: Dawn revealing trees closely packed round lake

parts.note: firs are coniferous trees

indicators.note: round shows the word for closely packed goes around the letter for lake

parts.note: tight means closely packed
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Daybreak shows trees crowded around a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts TIGHT around L, giving TLIGHT; 'revealing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Daybreak is when the first glimmer of the sun appears.

clue.text: Check cloak

explanation.surface: Inspect a cape.
explanation.definitionFit: To vet or examine people is one sense; a covering that hides something, as a smokescreen, is the other.

clue.text: Newly appointed Alec put in charge

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the letters are freshly arranged, appointed in a new order

explanation.surface: Alec, recently promoted, has been put in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newly appointed' reads as a job title but signals that ALEC PUT is rearranged to CULPATE, which follows IN.
explanation.definitionFit: To incriminate or blame someone is to lay a charge against them.

clue.text: Left warm den

parts.note: to air clothes is to warm them

explanation.surface: Someone has left a cosy room.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's den is its lair, the hidden home of a wild beast.

clue.text: Record-holder reportedly quit after close of Olympics

indicators.note: after places the homophone of quit behind the closing letter
the close of a word is its last letter, here of Olympics
reportedly means the word for quit is said aloud rather than spelt

parts.note: to leave is to quit

explanation.surface: A champion's said to be retiring after the Olympics end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record-holder' suggests an athlete, but the record is a vinyl disc and its cover holds it.
explanation.definitionFit: A vinyl disc is kept in a paper or card cover.

clue.text: Project totally different from sit-in?

explanation.surface: A plan unlike a sit-down protest.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition works word by word: stand is the opposite of sit and out the opposite of in.
explanation.definitionFit: To protrude or project is one sense; reversing each half of sit-in gives a phrase with the other sense of excelling.

clue.text: Unable to stand much more?

parts.note: the phrase suggests a person at the end of their patience, but describes a building so decrepit it is falling apart

explanation.definitionFit: A dilapidated, ramshackle building may soon collapse.

clue.text: Asian monkey's pronounced inactivity

indicators.note: pronounced signals that the word for inactivity is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: languor is listlessness or inactivity

explanation.surface: An Asian monkey is notably lazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pronounced' looks like an adjective (marked), but it is the homophone signal; the 's is a link meaning is.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a long-tailed leaf-eating primate of South and Southeast Asia.

clue.text: A timber used in renovating home and barn

indicators.note: renovating rebuilds something, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some wood has been used to do up a house and barn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'renovating' shuffles HOME and BARN together; 'and' only joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a hardwood tree whose very tough wood is used for timber.

clue.text: Wind and last of rain buffeted the lorry

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, here of rain
buffeted means knocked about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Wind and rain battered the truck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buffeted' rearranges THE LORRY into ORTHERLY after the N from 'last of rain'.
explanation.definitionFit: A breeze coming from the north is so described.

clue.text: Unlikely perpetrator of matchless crime?

parts.note: matchless seems to mean unrivalled, but read literally means without matches, which a fire-raiser would need

explanation.definitionFit: A fire-raiser can hardly commit the offence with no matches.

clue.text: German broods, and puts on a brilliant show

parts.note: litters are broods of young animals

explanation.surface: A German raises young and makes a dazzling display.
explanation.definitionFit: To sparkle or shine brightly is to make a brilliant show.

clue.text: New arrival incorporated more changes

indicators.note: changes shows the letters of more are rearranged

explanation.surface: A newcomer brings in further alterations.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has recently moved into an area is a newcomer.

clue.text: Tour with tenor and composer

parts.note: Maurice Ravel was a French composer

explanation.surface: A tour with a tenor and a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: To journey around a region is to tour it.

clue.text: Silver mine's infested by rats, say

indicators.note: a mine infested by something holds it within, so the letters sit inside the words

explanation.surface: A silver mine is overrun by rodents.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is silVER MINe, taken from inside the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Rats are a typical example of pests.

clue.text: Place for horseman's gear is secure to some extent

parts.note: to tack is to fasten or secure
room means scope or extent

explanation.surface: A stable store is fairly safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to some extent' looks like a hidden-word signal, but 'some extent' is ROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Saddles and bridles, known as tack, are kept in this stable store.

clue.text: Tackle I'd found in stern

parts.note: rig means equipment or tackle
taken as written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Fishing tackle discovered at the back of a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stern' sounds nautical, but it is an adjective meaning strict.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbending and strict, as a stern disciplinarian is.

clue.text: Split in Spades? Tough squeezing East

parts.note: S is the card abbreviation for spades

indicators.note: squeezing means the word for tough presses around the letter for east

parts.note: hard means tough

explanation.surface: A bridge player splits in spades and finds it hard against East.
explanation.definitionFit: Something split between people is divided among them.

clue.text: Speeds up, resulting in puncture

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: bats means moves fast, as in going at a rate of bats

explanation.surface: Hurrying causes a flat tyre.
explanation.walkthrough: BATS reads upwards as STAB; 'resulting in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To stab is to pierce or make a hole in.

clue.text: Primarily, self-satisfied fool is this

indicators.note: primarily means first, so the opening letter of self-satisfied is taken

parts.note: a mug is a dupe or fool

explanation.surface: A fool who is self-satisfied first and foremost is this.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a fool who is pleased with himself is complacent.
explanation.definitionFit: Being complacent and pleased with oneself is the meaning.

clue.text: Pump I've repaired for use in bad winter

indicators.note: the repaired letters are put to use inside the other word
bad means the letters of winter are disordered
repaired means put back together in a new order, so the letters of I've are rearranged

explanation.surface: A water pump I have fixed for a harsh winter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' makes INTERW from WINTER and 'repaired' makes VIE from I'VE, which goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To pump someone for information is to question them closely.

clue.text: At sea, directly taking seaman aboard, in praiseworthy way

indicators.note: taking with aboard means the seaman is held inside the jumbled word
at sea means confused, so the letters of directly are muddled

parts.note: AB is an able seaman

explanation.surface: Sailing straight with a sailor on board, admirably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' rearranges DIRECTLY into CREDITLY, and 'taking seaman aboard' puts AB inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something laudably earns credit.
